newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's parliament approves Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel's parliament approves Hebron deal.

text.p: Israel's parliament, in a rare display of unity, approved the Israel-PLO deal on Hebron on Thursday, opening the way for the start of an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town.

The main opposition Labour party and left-wing and Arab factions joined with most members of the ruling Likud coalition to vote 87-17, with one abstention for the U.S.-brokered accord sealed on Wednesday.
The televised vote came at the end of a 12-hour debate on the deal to pull Israeli soldiers out of most of Hebron and carry out three further redeployments from mainly rural areas of the West Bank.

The parliamentary resolution approved "the agreement signed between the government of Israel and the Palestinian Authority on January 15, 1997, in accordance with the documents and accompanying letters presented to it".
Prime Minister Benjanin Netanyahu said the Knesset decision would help move Israel towards "peace and security with the Palestinians".

"I thank the members of the house, I hope in the future, during this government's term, to bring complete peace agreements with the Palestinians and perhaps with Arab nations, in addition to the ones we have signed," he told parliament.

Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said earlier that Israel's troop redeployment from much of Hebron would start after the Knesset voted its approval and that he hoped to complete the pullback by Friday evening.

Hundreds of Palestinians were gathered outside Israeli military headquarters in Hebron, where soldiers had been removing equipment for most of the day. But there was no immediate Israeli move out of the building after the parliament vote.
